Subject: Quick recap + 2 asks from today's demo

Hi Aisha — thanks for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and two asks so we can model price scenarios for PulseHealth: 

1) Volumes: you mentioned "~12M tokens/day (mix of chat + completion) with 90% short form notes and 10% long form summaries". Can you confirm weekly and monthly averages + any seasonality?

2) Budget & target: you said the team is aiming for a target cost in the low- to mid-$ per 1M tokens range for production. Can you put a numeric band on "low-mid" for us? E.g., $300-$600/1M or $600-$900/1M?

What we'll deliver after we get those numbers: a short benchmarking sheet that compares Redwood hosted target vs OpenAI/Anthropic and two open-host providers under three volume tiers, and a suggested pilot pricing anchor for procurement conversations.

Attachments: I will include the benchmarking template and a sample term sheet in my next note.

Next steps: if you can reply with (A) monthly token avg, (B) a preferred $/1M band, (C) any hard SLAs or retention constraints, I'll produce the benchmark by EOD.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + 2 asks from today's demo

Diego — thanks for the recap. Confirming the numbers from our side: 

- Monthly avg: ~360M tokens/month (12M/day * ~30 days). We have a 20% monthly bump expected around open enrollment windows (Nov/Dec).
- Mix: roughly 90% short (<=256 tokens) / 10% long (>1k tokens).
- Target budget: procurement asked us to aim for $500/1M as the negotiation anchor; leadership is comfortable up to $750/1M but would prefer to land below $600/1M for FY27 planning.
- SLA/retention: 99.9% uptime target, 30-day request logs retention is required for audit.

Please include burst concurrency assumptions — we expect short spikes to ~2.5x daily average for a 2-3 hour window.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of AI Product, PulseHealth

Aisha — perfect, thanks for the clear numbers. I attached the benchmarking workbook (1m-token-benchmark.xlsx) and a draft term sheet (pulsehealth-term-sheet-v1.pdf). Highlights and assumptions baked into the sheet: 

- Scenarios: low (200M/mo), mid (360M/mo), high (450M/mo with 20% bump).
- Token mix weighting applied: cost modeled separately for short/long; long-form uses higher compute multiplier.
- External benchmark targets: OpenAI gpt-4-ish host list price, Anthropic Claude host list price, and two representative open-model hosts (quantized Llama variants on host A and host B).
- Redwood proposal: baseline pilot anchor at $480/1M for the first 3 months with an uplift schedule tied to committed monthly tokens; long-term committed pricing modeled down to $320/1M at 1.2B annualized commitment.
- SLA accommodations: 99.9% uptime is achievable on Dedicated; PV (private) option for audit requirements. Retention export can be configured to 30 days with req logs delivered to S3.

Quick ask: can procurement share preferred invoicing cadence (monthly or quarterly) and whether they require net-60 payment terms? I will also include burst-concurrency mitigation notes (prefetch/prefix caching + autoscale buffer) in the cost appendix.

Attachments: 1m-token-benchmark.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-provider slate), pulsehealth-term-sheet-v1.pdf (draft commercial terms).

I'll follow up internally to align the internal pricing owner and legal for redlines.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
